subject: math
title: Exponents and the Order of Operations
seo_title: Grade 6 Exponents Worksheets: Evaluate Powers and Use the Order of Operations
standard_text: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 exponents worksheets: write repeated multiplication as a power, evaluate powers of whole numbers, fractions and decimals, and use the order of operations with exponents. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: An exponent tells how many times to use the base as a factor: 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
key_sub: 2⁵ is not 2 × 5. In the order of operations, exponents come right after grouping symbols: 3 + 2³ × 2 = 3 + 8 × 2 = 19.
body_html:
What an exponent means

An exponent tells how many times to use a number as a factor. In 53, 5 is the base and 3 is the exponent. 53 = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. The whole thing is called a power.

PowerRead it asMeansValue
727 squared7 × 749
535 cubed5 × 5 × 5125
252 to the 5th power2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 232
10410 to the 4th power10 × 10 × 10 × 1010,000

Evaluate a power

Write the base as a factor as many times as the exponent says, then multiply.

Whole numbers

Evaluate 25 and 104.

25 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. For 104, write a 1 and 4 zeros: 10,000.

Answer: 32 and 10,000

Fractions and decimals

Evaluate (23)2 and 0.32.

(23)2 = 23 × 23 = 49. 0.32 = 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09 (2 decimal places in all).

Answer: 49 and 0.09

Any power of 1 is 1: 18 = 1. Any power of 0 is 0: 02 = 0 × 0 = 0.

The order of operations

StepDo thisExample
1Grouping symbols ( ), [ ], { }, the innermost first(4 + 2)2 = 62
2Exponents62 = 36
3× and ÷, from left to right36 ÷ 3 = 12
4+ and −, from left to right3 + 16 = 19

Many classes remember this as PEMDAS or GEMDAS (Grouping, Exponents, Multiply and Divide, Add and Subtract).

Example

Evaluate (4 + 2)2 ÷ 3.

(4 + 2)2 ÷ 3 = 62 ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12.

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
25 = 2 × 5 = 10Use 2 as a factor 5 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32
3 + 23 × 2 = 53 × 2Find the power before you add: 3 + 8 × 2 = 19
2 × 32 = 62 = 36The exponent is only on the 3: 2 × 9 = 18
(2 + 4)2 = 22 + 42 = 20Add inside the parentheses first: 62 = 36
0.32 = 0.90.3 × 0.3 = 0.09
104 = 1,000The exponent is the number of zeros: 10,000

faq.q: What is an exponent in 6th grade math?
faq.a: An exponent tells how many times to use the base as a factor. In 2⁵, the base is 2 and the exponent is 5, so 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.

faq.q: Where do exponents go in the order of operations?
faq.a: Exponents come right after grouping symbols and before multiplication and division. For example, 3 + 2³ × 2 = 3 + 8 × 2 = 3 + 16 = 19.
2⁵ means 2 used as a factor 5 times, not 2 × 5. 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. Multiplying the base by the exponent is the most common exponent mistake.

faq.q: How do you square a fraction or a decimal?

items.q: The cube is made of unit cubes, 4 on each edge. How many unit cubes make the cube?
items.e: 4<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. Not 16: that is only one face. Not 37: that counts only the cubes you can see.
10 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 10 and the exponent is 4: 10<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).

items.q: Which expression means the same as 93?
items.e: The exponent 3 says to use the base 9 as a factor 3 times: 9 × 9 × 9. It does not mean 9 × 3.
“Cubed” means an exponent of 3: 6<sup>3</sup> = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216. It is not 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 27?
items.e: The exponent 7 says to use the base 2 as a factor 7 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. It does not mean 2 × 7.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 64?
items.e: The exponent 4 says to use the base 6 as a factor 4 times: 6 × 6 × 6 × 6. It does not mean 6 × 4.
3 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 3 and the exponent is 4: 3<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).
An exponent of 2 is read “squared,” because 7<sup>2</sup> is the area of a square with sides of 7. “Cubed” is for an exponent of 3.
There are 2 factors of 5 and 3 factors of 7, so the expression is 5<sup>2</sup> × 7<sup>3</sup>. The factors are multiplied, so use ×, not +.
There are 3 factors of 2 and 2 factors of 3, so the expression is 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup>. The factors are multiplied, so use ×, not +.
Read the base first, then the exponent: 2<sup>5</sup> is “2 to the 5th power.” It means 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
5 is used as a factor 3 times, so the base is 5 and the exponent is 3: 5<sup>3</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 2 × signs).

items.q: In 83, which number is the base?
items.e: The base is the big number that is multiplied: 8. The small raised number 3 is the exponent. 8<sup>3</sup> = 8 × 8 × 8 = 512 is the value.

items.q: The square is 6 units long on each side. How many unit squares cover it?
items.e: 6<sup>2</sup> = 6 × 6 = 36. Not 12: that is 6 × 2. Not 24: that counts the units around the outside (the perimeter).
7 is used as a factor 4 times, so the base is 7 and the exponent is 4: 7<sup>4</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 3 × signs).

items.q: The square is 5 units long on each side. Which power shows how many unit squares cover it?
items.e: 5 rows of 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 5<sup>2</sup> = 25 unit squares. That is why an exponent of 2 is called “squared.”

items.q: The cube is made of unit cubes, 5 on each edge. Which power shows how many unit cubes make it?
items.e: Each layer has 5 × 5 cubes and there are 5 layers: 5 × 5 × 5 = 5<sup>3</sup> = 125. That is why an exponent of 3 is called “cubed.” 5<sup>2</sup> = 25 counts only one face.

items.q: Which expression means the same as 35?
items.e: The exponent 5 says to use the base 3 as a factor 5 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. It does not mean 3 × 5.

items.q: In 46, what does the exponent 6 tell you?
items.e: The exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor: 4<sup>6</sup> = 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 × 4. It is not 4 × 6.
2 is used as a factor 6 times, so the base is 2 and the exponent is 6: 2<sup>6</sup>. Count the factors, not the × signs (there are only 5 × signs).
0.2<sup>3</sup> = 0.2 × 0.2 × 0.2 = 0.008. 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, with 3 decimal places in all. Not 0.6: that is 0.2 × 3.

items.q: Which power has a value of 1,000?
items.e: 1,000 = 10 × 10 × 10 = 10<sup>3</sup>. The exponent is the number of zeros. 3<sup>10</sup> = 59,049 is much bigger.

items.q: What is the value of (12)3?
items.e: (12)3 = 12 × 12 × 12 = 18. Not 32: that is 12 × 3. Not 16: the denominator is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3.
2<sup>7</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 128. Not 14: that is 2 × 7, the base times the exponent.
1<sup>8</sup> = 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1. Any power of 1 is 1. 0<sup>2</sup> = 0 × 0 = 0, so it is not 2 or 1.
9<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 9 × 9 = 729. Not 27: that is 9 × 3, the base times the exponent.
4<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. Not 12: that is 4 × 3, the base times the exponent.
0<sup>4</sup> = 0 × 0 × 0 × 0 = 0. Not 4: that is 0 + 4. 1<sup>4</sup> = 1 and 4<sup>1</sup> = 4.
2<sup>5</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. Not 10: that is 2 × 5, the base times the exponent.
7<sup>2</sup> = 7 × 7 = 49. Not 14: that is 7 × 2, the base times the exponent.
6<sup>2</sup> = 6 × 6 = 36. Not 12: that is 6 × 2, the base times the exponent.
10<sup>4</sup> = 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10,000: a 1 followed by 4 zeros. Not 40: that is 10 × 4.
5<sup>3</sup> = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Not 15: that is 5 × 3, the base times the exponent.

items.q: What is the value of (34)2?
items.e: (34)2 = 34 × 34 = 916. Not 68: that doubles the numerator and denominator. Square both the numerator and the denominator.

items.q: What is the value of (23)2?
items.e: (23)2 = 23 × 23. Multiply the numerators and the denominators: 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 3 = 9. Not 43: that is 23 × 2. Not 29: square the numerator, too.
3<sup>4</sup> = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Not 12: that is 3 × 4, the base times the exponent.
1.5<sup>2</sup> = 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25. Not 3: that is 1.5 × 2. Not 1.25: you cannot square the 1 and the 0.5 separately.
2<sup>5</sup> = 32 and 5<sup>2</sup> = 25, so 2<sup>5</sup> is greater. Switching the base and the exponent changes the value.
0.3<sup>2</sup> = 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09. 3 × 3 = 9, and there are 2 decimal places in all. Not 0.9: count the decimal places.
8<sup>2</sup> + 4<sup>2</sup> = 64 + 4<sup>2</sup> = 64 + 16 = 80. Not 24: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.

items.q: Which part of (5 − 2)2 × 4 do you work out first?
items.e: (5 − 2)<sup>2</sup> × 4 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 4 = 9 × 4 = 36. Grouping symbols come first, even before the exponent.

items.q: Which part of 20 − 2 × 32 do you work out first?
items.e: 20 − 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 20 − 2 × 9 = 20 − 18 = 2. The exponent comes first, before × and −.
8<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 5<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 25 = 39. Not 6: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.

items.q: Which part of 4 + 3 × 23 do you work out first?
items.e: 4 + 3 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 + 3 × 8 = 4 + 24 = 28. The exponent comes first, before × and +.
2 × 5<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 25 = 50. Not 100: that comes from working strictly left to right.
3<sup>2</sup> × 2<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 8 = 72. Not 36: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
10<sup>4</sup> × 5 = 10,000 × 5 = 50,000. Not 200: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
7 + 2<sup>3</sup> − 9 = 7 + 8 − 9 = 15 − 9 = 6. Not 720: that comes from working strictly left to right.
12<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4 + 8 = 144 ÷ 4 + 8 = 36 + 8 = 44. Not 14: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
(2 + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> = 36. Sofia squared each number, but the sum must be found first.
10 − 2<sup>3</sup> = 10 − 8 = 2. Sam multiplied the base by the exponent, but 2<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
5 × 3<sup>2</sup> − 8 = 5 × 9 − 8 = 45 − 8 = 37. Not 217: that comes from working strictly left to right.
3 × (1 + 2)<sup>2</sup> = 3 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 3 × 9 = 27. Not 7: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
(11 − 2)<sup>3</sup> = 9<sup>3</sup> = 729. Not 3: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
2 + (5 + 13)<sup>2</sup> = 2 + 18<sup>2</sup> = 2 + 324 = 326. Not 176: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
6<sup>3</sup> − 2 × 8 = 216 − 2 × 8 = 216 − 16 = 200. Not 1,712: that comes from working strictly left to right.
6 + 2<sup>3</sup> × 4 = 6 + 8 × 4 = 6 + 32 = 38. Not 2,048: that comes from working strictly left to right.
(8 + 2)<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4 = 10<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4 = 100 ÷ 4 = 25. Not 9: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 9 = 18. Grace multiplied 2 × 3 first, but the exponent comes first.
[4<sup>2</sup> + 3<sup>2</sup>] × 5 = [16 + 3<sup>2</sup>] × 5 = [16 + 9] × 5 = 25 × 5 = 125. Work from the inside out. Not 70: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
20 + [12<sup>2</sup> ÷ (6 − 3)] = 20 + [12<sup>2</sup> ÷ 3] = 20 + [144 ÷ 3] = 20 + 48 = 68. Work from the inside out. Not 41: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
1 + 3 × 23 = 32
items.e: (1 + 3) × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 4 × 8 = 32. Without parentheses, 1 + 3 × 2<sup>3</sup> = 25.
[(5 + 4)<sup>2</sup> − 6] ÷ 3 = [9<sup>2</sup> − 6] ÷ 3 = [81 − 6] ÷ 3 = 75 ÷ 3 = 25. Work from the inside out. Not 5: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.

items.q: Find the value of (12)3 + 38.
items.e: (12)3 + 38 = 18 + 38 = 12. Not 1 78: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
8<sup>2</sup> − [3 × (6 − 2)] = 8<sup>2</sup> − [3 × 4] = 8<sup>2</sup> − 12 = 64 − 12 = 52. Work from the inside out. Not 48: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
(4 + 3)<sup>2</sup> − 2<sup>2</sup> = 7<sup>2</sup> − 2<sup>2</sup> = 49 − 2<sup>2</sup> = 49 − 4 = 45. Work from the inside out. Not 9: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
10<sup>3</sup> × 0.45 = 1,000 × 0.45 = 450. Not 13.5: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
{2 × [6<sup>2</sup> − 8]} + 19 = {2 × [36 − 8]} + 19 = {2 × 28} + 19 = 56 + 19 = 75. Work from the inside out. Not 83: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
0.5<sup>2</sup> + 0.3 = 0.25 + 0.3 = 0.55. Not 1.3: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.

items.q:
Where do the parentheses go to make the equation true?
2 × 3 + 12 = 32
items.e: 2 × (3 + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 4<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 16 = 32. Without parentheses, 2 × 3 + 1<sup>2</sup> = 7.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 36?
items.e: (2 + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> = 36. Without the parentheses, 2 + 4<sup>2</sup> = 18.
[20 + (5 − 3)<sup>2</sup>] ÷ 4 = [20 + 2<sup>2</sup>] ÷ 4 = [20 + 4] ÷ 4 = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Work from the inside out. Not 4: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
(0.3 + 0.1)<sup>2</sup> × 5 = 0.4<sup>2</sup> × 5 = 0.16 × 5 = 0.8. Not 0.35: that comes from skipping the parentheses.
2 × [5<sup>2</sup> − (3 + 1)] = 2 × [5<sup>2</sup> − 4] = 2 × [25 − 4] = 2 × 21 = 42. Work from the inside out. Not 46: that comes from skipping the inner grouping symbols.
12 × (12)2 = 12 × 14 = 3. Not 36: that comes from working strictly left to right.
4 × 0.2<sup>2</sup> = 4 × 0.04 = 0.16. Not 0.64: that comes from working strictly left to right.

items.q: Which expression has a value of 54?
items.e: 2 × (1 + 2)<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 3<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 27 = 54. Without the parentheses, 2 × 1 + 2<sup>3</sup> = 10.
1.2<sup>2</sup> − 0.44 = 1.44 − 0.44 = 1. Not 1.96: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.
(23)2 × 9 = 49 × 9 = 4. Not 12: that comes from multiplying the base by the exponent.

items.q: A small box is a cube with edges 12 ft long. What is its volume?
items.e: (12)3 = 12 × 12 × 12 = 18 cu ft. Not 32: that is 12 × 3. Not 14: that is only (12)2.

items.q: A square photo has 5 in sides. It is enlarged so the sides are 10 in. How many times as large is the area now?
items.e: Old area: 5<sup>2</sup> = 25 sq in. New area: 10<sup>2</sup> = 100 sq in. 100 ÷ 25 = 4, so 4 times as large. The sides double, but the area is 2<sup>2</sup> = 4 times as large.

items.q: A box is a cube with edges 6 in long. What is its volume?
items.e: Volume of a cube = edge × edge × edge = 6<sup>3</sup> = 216 cu in. Not 18: that is 6 × 3. Not 36: that is 6<sup>2</sup>, only one face.

items.q: A square garden is 9 ft long on each side. What is its area?
items.e: Area of a square = side × side = 9<sup>2</sup> = 81 sq ft. Not 18 sq ft: that is 9 × 2. 36 is the perimeter in feet.

items.q: A square patio is 12 tiles long and 12 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
items.e: 12<sup>2</sup> = 12 × 12 = 144 tiles. Not 48: that is the perimeter, 4 × 12. 1,728 is 12<sup>3</sup>.

items.q: A puzzle cube is made of small cubes, 3 on each edge. How many small cubes make the puzzle?
items.e: 3<sup>3</sup> = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 small cubes. Not 19: that counts only the cubes you can see. Not 54: that counts the squares on all 6 faces.

items.q: Kai puts a square rug with 6 ft sides on a floor that is 10 ft by 12 ft. How many square feet of the floor are not covered?
items.e: 10 × 12 − 6<sup>2</sup> = 10 × 12 − 36 = 120 − 36 = 84 sq ft. Not 108 sq ft: that uses 6 × 2 for the rug. Not 156 sq ft: subtract the rug, do not add it.

items.q: A school has 5 buildings. Each building has 5 floors, each floor has 5 classrooms, and each classroom has 5 windows. How many windows are there?
items.e: 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5<sup>4</sup> = 625 windows. Not 125: that is 5<sup>3</sup>, the number of classrooms.

items.q: A box holds 10<sup>3</sup> paper clips. How many paper clips are in 6 boxes?
items.e: 6 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 6 × 1,000 = 6,000 paper clips. Not 216,000: that is (6 × 10)<sup>3</sup>. Not 180: 10<sup>3</sup> is 1,000, not 30.

items.q: An amoeba splits into 2 amoebas every hour, and each new amoeba does the same. You start with 1 amoeba. How many amoebas are there after 6 hours?
items.e: Each hour the number doubles: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2<sup>6</sup> = 64. Not 12: that is 2 × 6. Not 32: that is only 5 hours.

items.q: A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares. Which expression shows the number of squares?
items.e: 8 rows of 8 is 8 × 8 = 8<sup>2</sup> = 64 squares. 2<sup>8</sup> = 256 and 8 × 2 = 16 are different.

items.q: Owen puts 1 penny in a jar on day 1, 2 pennies on day 2, 4 pennies on day 3, and keeps doubling. How many pennies does he put in on day 10?
items.e: From day 1 to day 10 the amount doubles 9 times, so day 10 is 2<sup>9</sup> = 512 pennies. Not 1,024: that is one doubling too many.

items.q: A lab dish has 5 bacteria. The number of bacteria doubles every day. How many bacteria are there after 4 days?
items.e: 5 × 2<sup>4</sup> = 5 × 16 = 80. Find the power first. Not 10,000: that is (5 × 2)<sup>4</sup>. Not 160: that is 5 days.

items.q: A square tile has sides of 0.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: 0.5<sup>2</sup> = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 sq m. Not 1 sq m: that is 0.5 × 2. Not 2.5: count the decimal places (2 in all).

items.q: Jack folds a sheet of paper in half 5 times. Each fold doubles the number of layers. How many layers are there now?
items.e: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2<sup>5</sup> = 32 layers. Not 10: that is 2 × 5. Not 25: that is 5<sup>2</sup>.

items.q: A square field has sides of 100 m. What is its area?
items.e: 100<sup>2</sup> = 100 × 100 = 10,000 sq m, which is 10<sup>4</sup>. Not 200: that is 100 × 2. Not 400: that is the perimeter.

items.q: A square garden with 8 m sides has a square pond with 3 m sides in it. What is the area of the garden without the pond?
items.e: 8<sup>2</sup> − 3<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 3<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 9 = 55 sq m. Not 25 sq m: that is (8 − 3)<sup>2</sup>. Square each side first, then subtract.

items.q: Two boxes are cubes. One has 4 in edges and the other has 5 in edges. What is their total volume?
items.e: 4<sup>3</sup> + 5<sup>3</sup> = 64 + 5<sup>3</sup> = 64 + 125 = 189 cu in. Not 729 cu in: that is (4 + 5)<sup>3</sup>. Find each volume first, then add.

items.q: Ava has 2 square rugs. Each one has 3 ft sides. What is the total area of the rugs?
items.e: 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> = 2 × 9 = 18 sq ft. Not 36 sq ft: that is (2 × 3)<sup>2</sup>. Find the power first, then multiply.

items.q: Zoe sends a message to 3 friends. In the next round, each of them sends it to 3 new friends, and so on. How many people get the message in round 4?
items.e: Round 1: 3. Round 2: 3<sup>2</sup> = 9. Round 3: 3<sup>3</sup> = 27. Round 4: 3<sup>4</sup> = 81. Not 12: that is 3 × 4.
